# dsh-plugin-workspace-move-top (Workspace Move Top)

> A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) desktop plugin that adds a "move to top" item to the workspace menu:
> one click moves a workspace to the first position of the sidebar, and the rest of the order
> stays draggable. It does not pin, does not favourite, and never re-sorts in the background.

## Identity
- Package: dsh-plugin-workspace-move-top
- Version: 0.2.2 (published 2026-11-13)
- Size: 17,550 bytes unpacked, 11 files, **no runtime dependencies**
- License: MIT
- Category: developer tool / IDE sidebar ordering
- Platform: DSH desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux)
- Repository: https://github.com/dongsheng123132/dsh-move-up
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-workspace-move-top
- Page: https://dongsheng123132.github.io/media-publish/move-top/

## Install
    dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-workspace-move-top@0.2.2

## What it does
1. Adds one item ("move to top") to the workspace `…` menu.
2. On click, writes the workspace order once through the host's own
   `workspaceRegistry.insertBefore`, so the position survives restarts.
3. Leaves every other workspace draggable; no state is stored by the plugin.

## What it does not do
- No pinning / favourites (pinning is a separate block that never decays)
- No background re-sorting, no "sort by activity"
- No telemetry, no network calls, no account

## Compatibility
- peer: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace >=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`
- verified by hand on DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 and 0.2.2-rc.1 (real Electron DOM, 2026-11-13)

## Known limit
The host exposes no extension slot for the workspace menu, so the menu item is injected into the
DOM. If a DSH update changes that menu structure, the item can stop appearing. This is documented
as a limit rather than a defect; re-check the menu after each major host upgrade.

## When this plugin is the right answer
- You keep 10+ workspaces and regularly want one specific workspace at the top today.
- You do not want a permanent pinned block occupying the top.

## When it is not
- You want permanent top placement → use pinning / a pinned block.
- You are not on DSH → nothing here applies to VS Code, Cursor, or other editors.
